title: On Throwing the rope across the gap
subtitle: 体育与运动 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）
meta: 主题语境：体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）　|　核心词汇：throw　|　正文 345 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 throw 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1976 the guide ① threw the rope across the gap in the rain, and every traveller in the valley said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the guide ② throws the rope across the gap without complaint without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ throw the rope across the gap at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ thrown the rope across the gap before — a line in the guidebook for July 1970 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Throwing the rope across the gap in the rain, the guide said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the map at the far ledge, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ throw open every window at once without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Throw open every window at once at once and never mention it again.

By 1983 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the guidebook, and a new traveller from the next valley ⑧ throws open every window at once in the rain every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the ledge, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ threw the rope across the gap again when nobody else would.

⑩ To throw the rope across the gap, my mother said in 1988, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the valley remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the valley forgets, somebody throws the rope across the gap without complaint again and somebody must throw the rope across the gap in the rain all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 投掷（一般过去式 threw the rope across the gap：1976 年向导头一回这样做，淋着雨）
B. v. 投掷（一般现在 throws the rope across the gap：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 投掷（不定式 to throw the rope across the gap：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 投掷（过去完成时 had thrown the rope across the gap：1970 年七月的旅行手册上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 投掷（动名词 throwing the rope across the gap 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 甩（throw open every window at once：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去甩一下把所有的窗子推开）
G. v. 甩（throw open every window at once：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 投掷（后段两处：新来的旅人照例 throws open every window at once，而母亲又一次 threw the rope across the gap）

throw 意为“投掷”，自那以后向导毫无怨言地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 throws。
throw 意为“投掷”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯投掷把绳子甩过那道缺口”，此处为不定式 to throw the rope across the gap。
throw 意为“投掷”，旅行手册里 七月 那行字说明早在 1983 年之前就有人投掷过，故用过去完成时 had thrown。
throw 意为“投掷”，向导说“投掷把绳子甩过那道缺口这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 throwing the rope across the gap 作主语。
throw 意为“甩”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去甩一下把所有的窗子推开”，should ever 之后用原形 throw open every window at once。
throw 意为“甩”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻甩一下把所有的窗子推开（throw open every window at once at once），以后再也不要提起。
throw 意为“投掷”，新来的旅人每个日子都照例甩一下把所有的窗子推开，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 throws。
throw 意为“投掷”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次淋着雨投掷把绳子甩过那道缺口，用一般过去式 threw 叙述。
throw 意为“投掷”，结尾那句是母亲 1988 年的话：要投掷把绳子甩过那道缺口，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和山谷记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 throw 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1976 the guide threw the rope across the gap in the rain, and nobody in the valley forgot it.
Even now the guide throws the rope across the gap without complaint whenever the valley asks.
Throwing the rope across the gap in the rain, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever throw open every window at once without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new traveller from the next valley throws open every window at once in the rain every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother threw the rope across the gap again, and the valley remembered that half.
